concerns.text: The plan uses asymptotic normal confidence intervals for N ≥ 1000 and a 200‑resample bootstrap for N < 1000 (see ‘Confidence intervals: asymptotic normal for N ≥ 1000; bootstrap (200 resamples) default for N < 1000’). Under model misspecification the AIPW estimator can exhibit non‑regular asymptotics, making the normal approximation unreliable and a 200‑resample bootstrap potentially insufficient for accurate 95 % coverage. This threatens the validity of SC‑003 (empirical coverage) and may lead to misleading conclusions about the double‑robust property.

The plan asserts that the full 27 000 Monte‑Carlo replications (including 1 000 replications per grid cell) will complete in ≤ 6 h on a standard GitHub Actions runner (2 CPU cores, ≤ 7 GB RAM). However, for the N = 500 cells the AIPW estimator uses a bootstrap with 200 resamples per replication, which multiplies the computational load by roughly 200× for those cells. This additional overhead is not accounted for in the runtime estimate and is likely to exceed the 6‑hour CPU limit, making the proposed compute strategy infeasible under the free‑compute constraints.

new_concerns.text: The plan asserts that HC3 robust variance provides asymptotically valid 95 % confidence intervals under model misspecification for all sample sizes (including N = 500). Robust variance estimators do not guarantee correct finite‑sample coverage when models are misspecified, especially at smaller N, which may jeopardize SC‑003 (empirical coverage) and the validity of conclusions about double‑robustness.
